transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
House Republicans quashed an effort tonight to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
in a near party-line vote.
The House voted to send the articles of impeachment filed by outgoing Kentucky Republican Congressman
Thomas Massie to committee, effectively killing the effort.
President Trump has stood by Hegseth, but many Republicans blame the Iran War for their
election losses, and Piers Tom Bowman says the vote comes after Hegseth delivered a defiant
defense.
He said all these military missions were lawful, and he noted that past presidents were never
called to task for their own operations at some question whether they violated the War
Powers Act.
Most of these impeachment articles have to do with the wars in Iran and Yemen.
By the way, he called Congressman Thomas Massie a "disgruntled, defeated congressman" and
talk of impeachment is a farce, a show trial.
NPR's Tom Bowman reporting, "Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders says he won't support Chuck
Schumer as the Democratic majority leader in the new Congress.
It sets up a confrontation after the party's sweep to power.
Meanwhile, congressional Republicans elected Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan to be the House
minority leader, and South Dakota Senator John Thune will continue to lead the party
in the Senate just no longer in the majority.
Four states are suing to stop rules tying Medicaid coverage to work.
Estimates are that more than 5 million people could lose coverage if the rules go into effect
in January," Alex Olgin reports.
Oregon, Minnesota, New Mexico, and Washington are alleging the new rules that require proof
of work, school, or volunteering to keep health insurance, fundamentally change the Medicaid
program, and cause states irreparable financial and public health harms.
The clock is ticking as the new eligibility rules are set to start in eight weeks.
This and other lawsuits that are delaying portions of these work requirements could
buy time for Democrats to reverse them when they take control of the House and Senate
next year.
Party leaders have already announced plans to overturn the Medicaid cuts and restore
generous Affordable Care Act tax credits.
For NPR News, I'm Alex Olgin.
Shares and the chip-making company NVIDIA dropped sharply for a second day after the
company launched an investigation of its CEO, who had an extramarital affair with a woman
who might have been recruited to spy for China, NPR's John Ruich reports.
NVIDIA's share price dropped about 5.5 percent after falling more than 4 percent on Monday.
The route comes after a weekend announcement by the company that the board is investigating
CEO Jensen Huang.
Huang co-founded NVIDIA more than three decades ago and transformed it into one of the world's
most valuable companies.
NVIDIA makes chips that have been at the center of the AI revolution, and investors are now
pondering what the investigation might yield and what it could mean for Jensen Huang's
future at the company.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Emissions of heat-trapping carbon dioxide from the burning of fossil fuels decreased slightly
this year due to the Iran War.
It's only the third decrease in carbon pollution this century.
This is NPR.
Tennessee is seeking to block Krista Pike's attorneys from accessing the execution drug
pentobarbital using the 50-year-old inmate's botched execution on the grounds that it would
reveal the supplier.
If that happens, the state says it may lose access to the drug and would be unlikely to
find an alternative source.
A rancher and farmer in Washington state who defrauded companies out of more than 244 million
dollars of beef cattle and went to federal prison for it is back home, Cody Easterday
is now under home confinement, Northwest Public Broadcasting's Anna King has the details.
During his home confinement, Cody Easterday will be under federal supervision, but he's
back in the Columbia Basin in time for Thanksgiving.
The farmer rancher was sentenced to 11 years in prison back in 2022.
The 55-year-old was transferred to home confinement on November 2, overseen by the Bureau of Prison
Seattle Residential Reentry Management Office.
Easterday made up ghost cattle on paper from his Eastern Washington ranch.
He also gamed the cattle futures market.
It's one of the largest cattle frauds in U.S. history.
For NPR News, I'm Anna King in Richland, Washington.
The national average price for a gallon of regular gas has fallen below $4 a gallon for
the first time since July, $3.98.
Some experts are predicting more price drops in the coming weeks and states that suspended
their gas taxes like Indiana, Ohio, Georgia and North Carolina could see even more.
I'm Rylan Barton, this is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: House Republicans vote to send Hegseth impeachment articles to committee, effectively killing them
Bernie Sanders says he won't support Chuck Schumer as Senate Democratic majority leader
Jim Jordan elected House minority leader; John Thune to keep leading Senate Republicans
Oregon, Minnesota, New Mexico, and Washington sue to block Medicaid work requirement rules
Nvidia shares fall for second day after board investigates CEO Jensen Huang over affair
Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuel burning dip slightly in 2025 due to Iran War
